title: The Reality that will surely come.
subtitle: A name for the Day that cannot be avoided

row.title: it will surely happen
sub: promise and threat both come true

then: The surah opens with one word. Ibn Kathir says {idea}al-Haqqah is one of the names of the Day of Judgment{/idea}, because on it {idea}the promise and the threat will inevitably occur.{/idea} This was one of the earliest surahs in Makkah.
now: Your calendar is full of things that might happen. The trip, the interview, the wedding. {trap}Many will not go as planned.{/trap} {idea}One date is certain, though no one knows when.{/idea}
old: The Day of Judgment is something far off and vague.
new: It is the one event in my future that is completely certain.
try: Look at your plans for this week and add one thing you would do if you remembered that Day.

title: What is the Inevitable Reality?
subtitle: A question asked to make you stop
then: The word comes again, now as a question. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah declared the greatness of this matter.{/idea} Repeating it makes the listener in Makkah {reward}stop and wonder{/reward} before anything is explained.
now: A doctor sits down and says, we need to talk about your results. You stop scrolling. {idea}Some questions are meant to make you put everything down.{/idea} This is one of them.
old: I already know what the Day of Judgment is.
new: The question is asked so I stop and take it seriously again.
try: Sit for one minute today with no phone and ask yourself: what is that Day, for me?

title: What could make you truly know what it is?
subtitle: Something bigger than your imagination
then: The third line deepens the question: {idea}and what will make you know what al-Haqqah is?{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it is said to {idea}declare the greatness of this matter.{/idea} Then the surah begins to show it, through the nations that denied it.
now: You have seen storms on the news and felt a hospital wait. You think you can picture big things. {idea}This Day is bigger than any of it.{/idea} The verse humbles your imagination.
old: I can imagine what that Day will be like.
new: It is greater than anything I can picture, so I listen to what Allah tells of it.
try: Read the next few verses of this surah slowly, as if hearing them for the first time.

title: Thamud and 'Ad called the Striking Day a lie.
subtitle: Two strong nations who denied what was coming
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah then mentions {trap}the destruction of the nations that denied the Resurrection.{/trap} Thamud and 'Ad were strong peoples of the past. {idea}Their denial did not change what was real.{/idea}
now: You ignore the dentist's warning. You do not open the bill. {trap}Not looking feels like it makes it go away.{/trap} {idea}It does not, and the same is true of bigger things.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about it, it is not my problem yet.
new: Denying something does not stop it. Preparing does.
try: Open one thing you have been avoiding, a message or a bill, and take one step on it.

title: Thamud was ended by an overwhelming blast.
subtitle: Transgression that brought its own end
then: Qatadah said the overpowering thing was {trap}the shout{/trap} that silenced them. Mujahid and others said it means {trap}their sins and transgression.{/trap} Ibn Zayd pointed to another verse: Thamud denied through their transgression.
now: A habit grows from one night to every night. A temper that was once a flash becomes the whole house. {trap}What we allow to grow can become what overwhelms us.{/trap} {idea}It is easier to stop it small.{/idea}
old: Disasters come from outside, not from what I do.
new: Unchecked wrongdoing can be the very thing that brings ruin.
try: Name one small habit that is growing in the wrong direction. Cut it back once today.

title: 'Ad was ended by a cold, raging wind.
subtitle: A strong people undone by the air
then: Ad-Dahhak said sarsar means {trap}cold{/trap}, and 'atiyah means it blew fiercely {trap}without any mercy or blessing.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said he was helped by an easterly wind, and 'Ad were destroyed by a westerly one.
now: You feel safe behind your walls, your insurance, your strong body. Then one storm, one virus, one night changes everything. {idea}Even the wind is under Allah's command.{/idea}
old: I am strong enough to handle whatever comes.
new: My strength is borrowed. The same air I breathe is in Allah's hands.
try: Next time you feel the wind today, remember who sends it and say alhamdulillah for safety.

title: Seven nights, eight days, and the mighty fell like trunks.
subtitle: How long it lasted and what was left
then: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and others said the days came {trap}in succession{/trap}, one after another. Ibn Abbas said hollow means {trap}ruined.{/trap} The people who had boasted of their strength {idea}lay like empty palm trunks.{/idea}
now: The tallest tower, the strongest company, the person everyone feared. {trap}Height and strength can be hollow inside.{/trap} {idea}What stands is what is rooted in Allah.{/idea}
old: Being big and strong means I will last.
new: Strength without faith can be hollow, however tall it stands.
try: Think of one way you show off strength. Replace it today with one quiet act of humility.

title: Do you see any of them left?
subtitle: A people gone without a trace
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do you find any one of them left{/trap}, or anyone who even claims to be from them? {trap}They are all gone{/trap}, and Allah left them no successors.
now: Search an old social network you used ten years ago. Most of it is gone. Names, pictures, fame. {trap}Things vanish faster than we think.{/trap} {idea}What you send ahead to Allah does not.{/idea}
old: People will remember me and what I built.
new: Names fade. What lasts is what I did for Allah.
try: Do one good deed today that you will never mention to anyone.

title: Pharaoh and the overturned cities came with the same sin.
subtitle: Different nations, one shared error
then: Ibn Kathir says al-khati'ah means {trap}their rejection of what Allah revealed.{/trap} Ar-Rabi' said it means disobedience. Pharaoh's people and {trap}the cities that rejected their messengers{/trap} all shared it.
now: Different people, different lives, the same root: I know better than what Allah said. {trap}It shows up in a boardroom, a bedroom, a group chat.{/trap} {idea}Check your own heart for the root, not just the branches.{/idea}
old: My mistakes are all separate little things.
new: Many wrongs grow from one root: putting my view above Allah's word.
try: Pick one area where you quietly think you know better than Allah. Ask Him for humility in it.

title: They disobeyed their messenger, and the seizure was severe.
subtitle: Rejecting one messenger is rejecting them all
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they all denied the messenger sent to them.{/trap} Only one messenger came to each nation, yet {idea}whoever denies a messenger denies all of them.{/idea} Mujahid said rabiyah means severe.
now: You hear a hadith you do not like and wave it off. You skip the part of the message that is inconvenient. {trap}Picking and choosing feels small.{/trap} {idea}The message is one whole.{/idea}
old: I can accept the parts I like and ignore the rest.
new: The message comes as a whole. Rejecting part of it is serious.
try: Find one teaching you have been avoiding. Learn one thing about why it was given.

title: When the flood rose, We carried you in the ship.
subtitle: Every human alive descends from the saved
then: Ibn Kathir says the water {trap}rose over its shores and overcame all that existed{/trap}, except those with Nuh in the ship. So {reward}all humans are from the loins of Nuh and his progeny.{/reward} That is why Allah says: We carried you.
now: You are here because, long ago, a few people were saved in a boat. Every person in your family tree survived something. {reward}Your existence is the end of a long chain of rescues.{/reward}
old: The flood is a story about other people.
new: I am alive because Allah carried my ancestors. It is my story too.
try: Thank Allah today for one specific ancestor or elder whose survival made your life possible.

title: A reminder for ears that hold on to it.
subtitle: Hearing that keeps what it hears

row.title: in one ear, out the other

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {reward}caused ships to remain for you{/reward}, so you ride the water and remember His blessing. The story is told so that {idea}a conscious ear would hold on to it.{/idea}
now: You board a ferry, see a cargo ship on the news, take a plane over the sea. {idea}Each one can be a small reminder of the ark.{/idea} You hear many reminders a day. {trap}Most slip away.{/trap}
old: I have heard these stories so many times already.
new: The goal is not to hear more, but to keep what I hear.
try: Pick one verse from today and repeat it to yourself three times before bed.
